blocks.text: Three containers for three kinds of talk

blocks.body: GitHub gives conversations a shape. An **[issue](about-issues)** tracks a unit of work — a bug, a task, a question with an owner and a lifecycle. A **[pull request](about-pull-requests)** proposes a change and carries its review. A **[discussion](about-discussions)** is the open-ended space for questions and ideas that are not yet work items. Choosing the right container is half the collaboration battle: work → issues, changes → pull requests, ideas → discussions.

rows: Trackable work — bugs, tasks, feature requests

blocks.body: A pull request can close the issue it fixes automatically: put a keyword — `closes`, `fixes`, or `resolves` — before the issue number in the PR body or a commit message ([linking a pull request to an issue](linking-pr-to-issue)). `Closes #12` in the description means merging the PR closes issue 12 — the trace the exam loves to test. Cross-references work too: mentioning `owner/repo#34` links across repositories.

blocks.text: Closing keywords only work from the default branch (usually `main`). If the PR targets a feature branch, the issue stays open after merge.

blocks.body: **Templates** pre-fill issue and PR bodies so reports arrive with the information you need — repro steps, screenshots, checklists. Keep them in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` or a `.github` repo for organization-wide defaults; see [about issue and pull request templates](issue-pr-templates). **Assignees** put a name on an issue or PR (up to ten); **filters** find everything else. The search bar is a query language:

blocks.code:
is:open is:issue author:octocat label:bug assignee:@me
draft:false is:pr review:approved

blocks.body: [Filtering and searching](filtering-issues) is worth ten minutes of play — the exam rarely asks syntax, but it does ask what filters can isolate (state, author, label, assignee, review status).

You participate, you get notified — [notifications](about-notifications) arrive for threads you author, are @mentioned in, or explicitly watch. Configure them per repo (watch all, just releases, or ignore) and globally in settings: email and/or the web inbox, and which events warrant each channel. A common exam framing: @mention in the body of a conversation notifies the person regardless of their watch settings on the repo.

blocks.text: The lighter surfaces: gists, wikis, Pages

items: **Gists** ([creating gists](about-gists)) — single-file snippets, public or secret; forkable and versioned like tiny repos.
**Wikis** ([about wikis](about-wikis)) — multi-page docs inside a repository; convenient but separate from the repo’s code history.
**GitHub Pages** ([what is Pages](about-github-pages)) — publishes a site straight from a repository on a chosen branch. This very site ships that way.
Issues track work, PRs propose changes, discussions hold ideas.
`Closes #12` in a PR targeting the default branch closes the issue on merge.
Templates live in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`; a `.github` repo sets org-wide defaults.
Notifications follow participation and watching; configure per repo and globally.
Gists for snippets, wikis for docs, Pages for published sites.
